Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher volume indices

Source: R/indice.R
fixed_weight_indices.Rd

Derive the Laspeyres-type, Paasche-type or Fisher-type volume indices of the total from the current prices and the price indices of its components.

Usage

laspeyres(
  cp,
  pi,
  output = c("index", "measure", "both"),
  reference_freq = 1,
  reference_cycle = NULL
)

paasche(
  cp,
  pi,
  output = c("index", "measure", "both"),
  reference_freq = 1,
  reference_cycle = NULL
)

fisher(
  cp,
  pi,
  output = c("index", "measure", "both"),
  all_index = FALSE,
  reference_freq = 1,
  reference_cycle = NULL
)

Arguments

cp

Current prices (ts or mts).

pi

Price indices (previous reference period = 100), same structure as cp.

output

Character if the output should be the volume index (the default), the volume measure (in monetary terms) or both.

reference_freq

Frequency of the reference period: 1 (default) for the previous year, or the frequency of the data (4 or 12) for the previous period (quarter or month). It must divide the frequency of cp.

reference_cycle

Integer to use a given period of the previous year as reference (the last period of the year, 4 for quarterly data or 12 for monthly data) instead of the average of the year, as needed for the one-quarter overlap technique. It is used with reference_freq equal to the frequency of cp. The reference period is valued at its own current prices: the one-quarter overlap technique of the manual values it at the average prices of the year, see chain_laspeyres() and cp_pi2cy().

all_index

(fisher() only) Boolean: if TRUE, return the Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher indices instead of the Fisher index only.

Value

A ts (or mts).

Details

With \(v_{i,t}\) the elementary volume index of the component \(i\) (cp_pi2vol()), \(w_{i,r}\) its share in the current prices of the total in the reference period \(r\) (the previous year, by default) and \(w_{i,c}\) its share in the current period \(c\) (the current year, by default): $$L_t = \sum_i w_{i,r}\, v_{i,t}, \qquad P_t = \left(\sum_i \frac{w_{i,c}}{v_{i,t}}\right)^{-1}, \qquad F_t = \sqrt{L_t P_t}.$$ The volume measure is the index times the value per period of the total in the reference period, divided by 100.

References

International Monetary Fund (2018), Quarterly National Accounts Manual (2017 Edition), chapter 8 "Price and Volume Measures", Washington, DC. doi:10.5089/9781475589870.069 .

Examples

# Laspeyres-type volume index over the previous year
laspeyres(imf_cp, imf_pi)
#>          Qtr1     Qtr2     Qtr3     Qtr4
#> 2011 100.7146 100.6082 100.6459 100.9588
#> 2012 100.4327 100.4151 100.9329 101.8548
#> 2013 101.9515 102.5155 102.4950 102.3481
# Volume index and measure (in monetary terms)
paasche(imf_cp, imf_pi, output = "both")
#>             Index  Measure
#> 2011 Q1 100.84230 381.9150
#> 2011 Q2 100.73235 381.4986
#> 2011 Q3 100.70951 381.4121
#> 2011 Q4 100.96596 382.3833
#> 2012 Q1 100.65838 384.6408
#> 2012 Q2 100.79021 385.1446
#> 2012 Q3 101.09097 386.2939
#> 2012 Q4  99.37475 379.7358
#> 2013 Q1 103.01329 402.8850
#> 2013 Q2 102.58697 401.2177
#> 2013 Q3 101.37238 396.4674
#> 2013 Q4 100.48494 392.9966
# The three indices
fisher(imf_cp, imf_pi, all_index = TRUE)
#>         Laspeyres   Paasche   Fisher
#> 2011 Q1  100.7146 100.84230 100.7784
#> 2011 Q2  100.6082 100.73235 100.6703
#> 2011 Q3  100.6459 100.70951 100.6777
#> 2011 Q4  100.9588 100.96596 100.9624
#> 2012 Q1  100.4327 100.65838 100.5455
#> 2012 Q2  100.4151 100.79021 100.6025
#> 2012 Q3  100.9329 101.09097 101.0119
#> 2012 Q4  101.8548  99.37475 100.6071
#> 2013 Q1  101.9515 103.01329 102.4810
#> 2013 Q2  102.5155 102.58697 102.5512
#> 2013 Q3  102.4950 101.37238 101.9321
#> 2013 Q4  102.3481 100.48494 101.4123
# Quarter-to-quarter indices need price indices over the previous quarter
fisher(imf_cp, pi_py2pp(imf_pi), reference_freq = 4)
#>           Qtr1      Qtr2      Qtr3      Qtr4
#> 2011 100.73654  99.92231 100.07836 100.33142
#> 2012 100.17546 100.06025 100.58254 101.06762
#> 2013 100.75625 100.53763  99.93702  99.82502
